text: Van den Dyck was known in Italy as Daniel Vandich. After training in Antwerp he left for Italy, where he first worked in Venice and later became a court painter in Mantua. He was versatile and made mythological and religious scenes, portraits and flower pieces. Very little is known about his early life. He was the son of Jan van den Dyck and Cornelia Kerstboom and was baptized in Antwerp Cathedral. He also worked as an architect and engineer.

A successful lawyer in Amsterdam, Asser could afford photography, a very expensive hobby at the time. His first daguerreotype experiments were reproductions of academic art. He is best known for his efforts to make photographic printing cheaper, above all his 1858 patent on the Procédé Asser, a photolithography process. He was an editor of a Dutch photography magazine and a member of the Amsterdam photographers' society Helios.

A founder member of the Royal Academy, Penny came from Knutsford in Cheshire, one of the twin elder sons of a surgeon. He was sent to London to study under Thomas Hudson and later went to Rome to study under Marco Benefial. He returned to England about 1748 and began his professional career by painting small whole-lengths. Later he painted more demanding subjects.

The fourth son of the engraver William Holl the Elder, Francis Holl was apprenticed to his father. His brother William Holl the Younger was an engraver too. He spent 25 years engraving Queen Victoria's pictures and executed commissions of other royal portraits as well. He often worked from paintings by fashionable artists and exhibited 20 engravings at the Royal Academy between 1856 and 1883.

Chantrey became the leading portrait sculptor in Regency Britain, producing busts and statues of many notable figures. His most notable works include the statues of King George IV in Trafalgar Square, King George III at the Guildhall, and George Washington in the Massachusetts State House. He also made four monuments to military heroes for St Paul's Cathedral. He left the Chantrey Bequest, a fund for buying works of art for the nation, which became available in 1877.

A realist painter, Tepa specialised in portraits and Orientalist themes. During the Revolutions of 1848 he became politically involved in the independence movement. He produced a series of portraits of Polish leaders of the November Uprising, among them Joachim Lelewel, Józef Dwernicki and Józef Chłopicki, and he was jailed as a political prisoner in Vienna. His father was a confectioner.

The son of the painter Adriaan Verwilt of Antwerp, Verwilt was apprenticed to Cornelis van Poelenburgh in Utrecht, along with Jan van der Lijs and others. He is considered part of the Poelenburch landscape school. Houbraken, who mentions him as a pupil of Poelenburch, says he painted the flesh tones of his figures in the manner of another pupil, Daniel Vertangen. He was a landscape painter in Rotterdam, where he was born and died.

Van Leemputten is known for landscapes of the Campine and Brabant regions and for genre scenes with villagers and animals. His father was originally a farmer but moved to Brussels in 1852 to become a painting restorer, because he had an interest in art. Frans and his older brother Cornelius were encouraged by their father to practise art. He was also a watercolorist and an art educator. Candle Procession in Scherpenheuvel is among his pictures.

A tax collector's son, Streitt graduated from the Realschule in Lviv and studied at the Technical University there. From 1856 to 1866 he studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Kraków with Władysław Łuszczkiewicz and Jan Matejko, and he finished at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna in 1871. He first settled in Kraków and painted historical scenes inspired by Matejko. He stayed only briefly before moving to Munich.

Scott worked as a war correspondent and illustrator for the French magazine L'Illustration. He painted the Balkan Wars and the First World War, and he also covered and illustrated scenes from the Spanish Civil War and the early Second World War. An oil painting of his showing King Constantine I of Greece during the Balkan Wars hangs in the main entry hall of the Presidential Palace in Athens. His work was part of the painting event in the art competition at the 1928 Summer Olympics.

Balducci was called Il Cosci, after his maternal uncle. He was trained in Florence by Giovanni Battista Naldini. He worked as an assistant to Federico Zuccari on the fresco of the Last Judgment inside Brunelleschi's dome of the Duomo in Florence, with Vasari supervising. He also frescoed a Last Supper in the church. He took part, too, in decorations for the wedding of Ferdinand I de' Medici.

A pupil of Portaels and then of Jean-Léon Gérôme, Wauters produced in 1868 The Battle of Hastings: the Finding of the Body of Harold by Edith. He journeyed to Italy, but his study of the old masters did not affect his individuality, as his Great Nave of St. Mark's showed; Leopold II of Belgium bought it. His youth kept him from the medal of the Brussels Salon, so the minister of fine arts sent him as artist-delegate to Suez by way of compensation.

Burnand's prosperous parents taught him to appreciate art and the countryside. He trained as an architect first. Painting was his real vocation. He studied art in Geneva and Paris and then settled in Versailles. In the course of his life he travelled widely and lived for a time in Florence, Montpellier, Seppey and Neuchâtel. He was primarily a realist painter of nature.

Born to artisan parents of limited means, Migliara was apprenticed to the sculptor Giuseppe Maria Bonzanigo. He also studied at the Brera Academy with Giocondo Albertolli. He began as a set designer at the Teatro Carcano and at La Scala, under Alessandro Sanquirico. Lung disease stopped him for a while. From 1810 he painted again, mostly miniatures in watercolours and oils.

Architect, decorator and painter to the French Imperial Court in Venice, Borsato was the son of an ornamental painter. He studied perspective with Agostino Mengozzi Colonna at the Accademia di Belle Arti, and he painted interiors of churches, sometimes in the manner of Canaletto. He was also influenced by his contemporary Vincenzo Chilone. In 1805 he decorated the Onigo theater in Treviso.

Marchant began his career as a house painter and was largely self-taught. By the mid-1820s he had a portrait studio in his home town, Edgartown, Massachusetts. He studied briefly with Gilbert Stuart in Boston in 1825 and became familiar with Stuart's style. He painted Henry Clay and George Washington. Late in 1826 he advertised his services in a Charleston, South Carolina newspaper.

A pastor's son, Oeri grew up in Kyburg and Regensdorf. From 1800 he was a pupil of the landscape painter Johann Kaspar Kuster. After two years of study he showed a self-portrait at an exhibition in Zürich and received praise from Johann Martin Usteri. In 1803 he travelled to Paris with his friend, the portrait painter David Sulzer, and spent four years studying with Jacques-Louis David. He worked as a portrait and history painter, draftsman and lithographer.

Bendien moved from Amsterdam to Paris in 1911, where he met the sculptor-painter John Rädecker and the painter Jan van Deene. Together they started making what they called Absolute art, a form of abstract art that grew from their joint Amsterdam show for De Onafhankelijken, the city's Independents art club, in 1913. According to the RKD he was the uncle of Eva Bendien, who later started the Galerie Espace, a modern art gallery in Haarlem and Amsterdam. He died of tuberculosis in Hilversum.

Raised in a Catholic family, Jurres was drawn from a young age to Catholic art and to military drills. At fifteen he went to Amsterdam to study art. He first had success when a series of his illustrations for Don Quixote was published in an edition of Cervantes' book. Contemporaries compared him with Rembrandt, Velázquez and Rubens, whose works influenced his style. In 1921 he became a professor at the Rijksakademie. His work is in the Rijksmuseum and the Fries Museum.

Carlson was known for his meditative winter scenes in the tonalist tradition. He co-founded the Woodstock School of Landscape Painting and later founded his own school there, the John Fabian Carlson School of Landscape Painting, in Woodstock, New York. In 1928 he wrote Elementary Principles of Landscape Painting, later reissued as Carlson's Guide to Landscape Painting. He was born in Västervik in Sweden. Brooding Silence is among his pictures.

Momper was active in Antwerp between the late 16th and early 17th centuries. Brueghel's influence is clearly evident in many of his paintings. His work stands at the transition from late 16th-century Mannerism to the greater realism in landscape painting that developed in the early 17th century. He achieved considerable success during his lifetime. His name came from his grandfather, a landscape painter.

Kapliński came from a Frankist family. His grandfather Eliasz Adam Kapliński was one of the last known Frankists, and his father, Jan, was a small landowner and an eminent freemason. Leon studied law and philosophy in Warsaw and Wrocław. He was engaged in revolutionary underground groups, fled the part of Poland under Russian rule, and was briefly held and interrogated by the Prussian police. He took part in the revolutionary movement in 1848.

Ludwig Dettmann grew up in Hamburg, where his father, a customs officer, was transferred when Ludwig was still a small child. After some studies at a local arts and crafts school, he moved to the Prussian Academy of Arts, where he studied with Eugen Bracht and Franz Skarbina. He first worked as an illustrator. After 1891 he was a teacher. Shortly before his death he was added to the Gottbegnadeten list, a roster of artists considered crucial to Nazi culture.

Pieter Oyens had an identical twin, David, and both brothers painted genre scenes. They spent most of their careers in Brussels. Their name was originally spelled Oijens. The twins were two of the ten children of a family of bankers, and from the age of eight they took drawing lessons, at the insistence of their mother, an amateur artist. They proved to be poor students, and they were not much more successful at learning the banking trade.

Born in Castelfranco Veneto, Damini was a pupil of the painter Giovanni Battista Novelli and was active in Venice. He painted Christ giving keys to Peter for San Clemente in Padua and a Crucifixion for the Basilica of St Anthony there. He also painted an image of Saint Prosdocimus. His Saints Prosdocimus, Justina, Daniel, and Anthony of Padua in Glory is among his works.

Lalique designed perfume bottles, vases, chandeliers, clocks and car hood ornaments as well as jewellery and glass art. He was born in Aÿ, in the Marne, to a traveling peddler. The family moved to the suburbs of Paris in 1862, but they went back to Aÿ for summer holidays, and those trips later influenced his naturalistic glasswork. At twelve he entered the Collège Turgot. His Pendant: wisteria dates from around 1900.

Graves came from a family of printsellers: his father and grandfather, both named Robert Graves, sold prints in London. In 1812 he became a pupil of the line engraver John Romney and also studied in the life school in Ship Yard, Temple Bar. He made pen and ink facsimiles of rare prints on commissions from collectors, and then decided to concentrate on engraving. In 1836 he was elected an associate engraver of the Royal Academy, in succession to James Fittler.

Monk, painter, calligrapher and master of the tea ceremony, Shōkadō Shōjō lived in the Edo period. Shōjō was the Buddhist name he was given when he entered the Hachiman shrine on Otoko-yama near Kyoto. He later served the Konoe family under Konoe Nobutada and came to know the Zen monks of Daitoku-ji. In 1627 he became head of the small Takimoto-bō temple, and ten years later he retired to a hut on the temple's estate.

Gaucherel learned art from his childhood friend Eugène Viollet-le-Duc, whom he accompanied to Sicily. His first major works were illustrations for a project to restore Notre-Dame, proposed in 1843 by Viollet-le-Duc and Jean-Baptiste Lassus. A year later he began etching. Over time he went from producing original engravings to making reproductions of works by other artists. By 1858 the transition was complete, and he began creating illustrations for magazines, notably the Gazette des Beaux-Arts.

De Fontenay's parents were said to belong to the French nobility, who had fled during the Revolution. His father, Anthonius Augustinus de Fontenay, was a soldier. His artistic training began at the technical school of the Maatschappij tot Nut van 't Algemeen in Amsterdam, and he also took lessons from the printmaker Jacob Smies. He worked as a painter, draftsman and lithographer, and he made a portrait miniature of Geertruida Anna Elisabeth Hoffmann.

The eldest son of the engraver Matthäus Merian the Elder, Merian the Younger was born in Basel and became an engraver too. His half-sister was Maria Sibylla Merian and his brother was Caspar. He is documented as importing wine and other luxury goods for Carl Gustaf Wrangel. He is known for his portraits, and he taught Bartholomäus Kilian. He also made a picture of his father's family.

Ykens regularly collaborated with specialist still life and landscape painters, providing the figures in their works. He was born in Antwerp, the son of a sculptor and painter, Johannes Ykens, and his second wife Barbara Brekevelt. His sister Catarina was a flower painter. His father trained him, and in the guild year 1673 to 1674 he was admitted as a master of the Antwerp Guild of Saint Luke, as a wijnmeester, the son of a master. He is mainly known for his history paintings and portraits.

A pupil of Claude Bonnefond at the fine arts school in Lyon, Comte moved to Paris to enter the studio of Joseph-Nicolas Robert-Fleury. He exhibited at the Salon in Paris for almost forty years. He won a third-class medal at the Salon of 1852, and later second-class medals. His works include The Oath of Henri de Guise and The Coronation of Inês de Castro.

Born and mainly active in Verona, Marcola was first apprenticed to his father Giovanni Battista Marcola. Among his pupils were Antonio Pachera and Bellino Bellini. He is also known as Marco Marcuola. His sister Angela Marcola was also a painter. He spent his career mostly in Verona. Among his pictures are Mercury and Mars, Harlequinade and Gaius Mucius Scaevola Thrusting His Right Hand into Fire.

Born Dommershuisen in Utrecht, the illegitimate son of Cornelia Dommershuisen, Dommersen was a painter and watercolourist who worked in England. His family had come from Dahlheim near Koblenz before 1700, and the name was originally Dommershausen. He was the elder brother of the painter Cornelis Christiaan Dommersen. He signed his work in several spellings of the name. He painted Dutch shipping.

Carr trained at the Royal School of Design in Chester, then moved to New York City in the early 1860s. He lived in Brooklyn from 1879 to 1907. There he developed an eerie style in which shapes were repeated again and again, then flipped or rotated, yet still looked lifelike. He lived with his sister Annie and her husband, John Bond, and never married.

Born in Watsonville, California, Dorgeloh studied at the California School of Fine Arts and at the State Teachers College at San Jose. She went on to work for the San Francisco Fine Arts Project of the Works Progress Administration. As a printmaker she took part in the WPA's Federal Art Project. Her prints include Pacific Cable Car, San Francisco, House and Garden, and Danish Church, San Francisco.

Hagen came from an old Rhenish merchant family in Düsseldorf, and from 1863 to 1868 he studied with Oswald Achenbach at the Kunstakademie there. In 1871 he was summoned to the art school in Weimar to teach landscape painting, as a replacement for Max Schmidt, who had left to take another position. Three years later he received a permanent appointment. He was head of the art department for five years but grew tired of the administrative duties and went back to teaching.

Masip was influenced by Paolo de San Leocadio and Rodrigo de Osona, and he is considered a Quattrocento painter. One of his early works was the altarpiece of Porta-Coeli, now in the Museu de Belles Arts de València. Between 1529 and 1532 he was responsible for the old high altar of Segorbe Cathedral, perhaps already with the help of his son Juan. His son was Vicente Juan Masip, and his grandson was Vicent de Joanes.

For a long time Stetter was known only as Master W. S. with the Maltese cross, until the scholar Jean Rott identified him in 1952. He was born and died in Strasbourg. As a painter he was influenced by Hans Baldung and Albrecht Dürer, and he was also a member of the Order of Saint John from 1510, first as an acolyte and then, from 1512, as a priest. His works are in the Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame in Strasbourg, the Unterlinden Museum in Colmar and the Walters Art Museum in Baltimore.

Bigg enrolled at the Royal Academy Schools in 1778 and studied under Edward Penny, who was best at depicting acts of charity. Bigg's greatest delight was painting children. His first work in this genre, shown in 1778, was Schoolboys giving Charity to a Blind Man. A year later he painted a similar work, A Lady and her Children relieving a Distressed Cottager. He later painted Christening of the Heir and Birth of the Heir.

Silva Porto studied in Porto and then continued in Paris and Rome. In Paris he exhibited at the Salon and at the World's Fair of 1878. There he studied with his friend João Marques de Oliveira, and both were pupils of Adolphe Yvon and Alexandre Cabanel. They became followers of the naturalist Barbizon School, and when they returned to Portugal in 1879 they brought the new school of painting with them.

Burgess painted historical and genre scenes, mainly in Spain, and can be counted as an English contributor to the Costumbrismo movement. His father, Henry William Burgess, was landscape painter to William IV, and the family had produced distinguished artists for several generations. After his father died when he was ten years old, he received art training from William Charles Ross. The Fan Seller and The Spanish Lady are among his pictures.

Eddy's father, Isaac Newton Eddy, was a printer, inventor and engraver, and he taught Oliver copper engraving. Oliver taught himself painting. In 1822 he married Jane Maria Burger in Newburgh, New York. In 1826 he moved to New York City, where he painted portraits and miniatures. His father moved the family from Vermont to Waterford, New York, that same year and started the Franklin Ink Works, which made printing inks.

Active in France until 1801, Duval worked as an artist and engraver. His earliest known work, from 1769, is a highly detailed watercolor of a dungeon, and a later dungeon watercolor is signed and dated 1773. A drawing for an oval, enamelled gold snuffbox in the Victoria and Albert Museum bears an identical signature. Engravings of his depictions of French furniture were published in Paris.

Raleigh ran away to sea at ten and boarded a naval ship commanded by his uncle. He served in the United States Navy during the Mexican-American War and later joined the merchant navy. In 1887 he married and settled in New Bedford, Massachusetts. He was a self-taught artist and an expert in ship portraits in the folk art tradition. He also painted houses.

Asam lived in Rome from 1711 to 1713 to study at the Accademia di San Luca with Carlo Maratta, and in 1713 he won the Academy's first prize for his drawing of Miracle of Saint Pio. In Germany he worked with his brother Egid Quirin, a stucco worker, on building and decorating entirely new churches, such as the Asam Church in Munich, and on redesigning churches in the Baroque style. One of those was the Benedictine monastery church of St. Emmeram in Regensburg.

Born Jeanne-Marie-Catherine Desmarquets in Paris, Auzou took the surname La Chapelle when a cousin adopted her. In December 1793 she married the stationer Charles-Marie Auzou, and from 1794 they had at least two sons and two daughters. She exhibited at the Paris Salon for almost twenty-five years. The Piano Lesson and Daria, or Maternal Terror are among her paintings. She died in Paris.
